what: Vornado Realty Trust owns office buildings and retail property, almost all of it in Manhattan. Its portfolio includes towers around Penn Station, where it is redeveloping a large district, plus retail space on Fifth Avenue and Times Square, and some property in Chicago and San Francisco.
customers: Corporate office tenants in New York, above all financial, legal and technology firms, and retailers leasing flagship space in Manhattan's best-known shopping streets.
money: Leases in Manhattan office towers, typically long-term.
Flagship retail on Fifth Avenue, Times Square and Penn District.
Hotel, trade show and management fee income.
moat: Irreplaceable locations. Vornado owns a concentration of property around Penn Station, Manhattan's busiest transport hub, and flagship retail on streets where there is no substitute address. Those sites cannot be recreated, which is why the properties retain value even through office downturns.
risks: The trailing twelve months show a net loss of about $52.9M, and revenue has been flat at $1.8B for four years.
Office demand in New York has not returned to pre-pandemic patterns, and older buildings in particular struggle to attract tenants.

Debt is about $3.0B at the corporate level with much more at the property level, and refinancing office buildings at current rates is expensive and in some cases impossible without putting in more equity.
The Penn District redevelopment requires enormous capital over many years before it produces income.
Retail rents on Fifth Avenue recovered strongly, but retail is a smaller share of the portfolio than office.
opportunities: The best Manhattan buildings have seen a genuine recovery in leasing as tenants consolidate into higher-quality space, and Vornado's core assets qualify.
Free cash flow of about $409.3M and $840.9M of cash provide room to wait out the cycle.
Penn District will eventually transform a neglected area next to the busiest transport hub in the country.
Thirteen analysts average a $39.15 target, about 18% above the current price.
watch: Office leasing volume and occupancy in the Manhattan portfolio. Everything else, including the long-term Penn District story, depends on whether tenants are signing leases now.
